key_insight: SocialOmni introduces a focused benchmark for evaluating audio-visual social interactivity in omni-modal LLMs, shifting evaluation from static accuracy to dynamic conversational competence across multimodal cues.
problem_solved: Existing omni-modal model benchmarks emphasize static, accuracy-centric tasks and fail to measure models' ability to interpret and respond to time-varying social signals in natural dialogues. SocialOmni fills this gap by operationalizing social interactivity evaluation for audio-visual-text models.
method: Define three core dimensions of conversational interactivity (e.g., temporal responsiveness, multimodal grounding, social appropriateness) and corresponding metrics.
Curate audio–visual conversational scenarios and annotation protocols that capture dynamic cues (speech prosody, gestures, gaze, turn-taking) and social responses.
Provide standardized evaluation suites and baseline OLM assessments to quantify strengths/weaknesses across the three dimensions.
impact: Enables practitioners and researchers to diagnose and improve omni-modal models' real-world conversational behavior, guiding development of systems that are more socially aware and reliable in interactive settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing data collection → annotation → evaluation metrics → benchmark scores
Tri-axis radar chart comparing model performance across the three social-interactivity dimensions

paper_title: SocialOmni: Benchmarking Audio-Visual Social Interactivity in Omni Models
paper_authors: Tianyu Xie, Jinfa Huang, Yuexiao Ma, Rongfang Luo, Yan Yang
